cf.title: BUG #19752: GROUP BY on a constant and a cast to a length-limited array type crashes the server while planning

input.subject: BUG #19752: GROUP BY on a constant and a cast to a length-limited array type crashes the server while planning

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal or the rule in v3. The fix addresses a reported planner crash on Postgres 18, and a committer agreed in message #2 that wrong answers are also possible. The one surviving objection, replication-ondisk-1, is a fixable back-patch point about views already stored on 18.x. The remaining risk is whether the new rule is correct in the grouping code, which needs a committer who knows that code.

brief.title: Stop replacing Var-free subexpressions with grouped Vars in GROUP BY
brief.problem: Since Postgres 18, `SELECT ARRAY[]::varchar(500)[] GROUP BY CAST('true' AS boolean)` crashes the planner with SIGSEGV. substitute_grouped_columns_mutator() replaces any Const that equal()s a GROUP BY item, including the internal isExplicit flag inside ArrayCoerceExpr.elemexpr, so constant folding later evaluates a Var with no tuple slot. Tom Lane notes that non-crash cases may give wrong answers.
brief.proposed_design: parseCheckAggregates() records which GROUP BY items contain no Vars of the current query level. For those items, only the targetlist entry that GROUP BY identified, matched by ressortgroupref, is replaced as a whole, and the items are skipped in the equal() loop at every sublevel. The early return for Const and Param moves back to the top of the mutator, as before f5050f795ae.
author_claims: The reported query no longer crashes.
`select 1 as one group by rollup(one) order by one nulls first` still returns a null row, then 1.
`select 1 as one, 1+2 as three group by rollup(one)` leaves three as 3.
In `select 1+2 as three, (1+2)*10 as x group by rollup(three)`, the 1+2 inside x is no longer replaced by a nullable grouped Var.
Postgres 17 is not affected; the bug comes from parse_agg.c changes in 18, not from clauses.c.
brief.thread_state: Matheus Alcantara reviewed the first patch and wrote v2, which follows Tom Lane's "none except the identified TLE" rule; Andrey Rachitskiy adopted it as v3 with a test fix after a cfbot failure. Tom Lane has not commented on any patch, despite a direct request.
unclear: The material does not say whether the fix is meant for back-patching to 18.
The patch prose covers only the first patch; v2 and v3 have no listed files or commit message.
The thread does not say whether skipping Var-free items at every sublevel changes results for correlated subqueries or outer references.
The thread does not show any check that existing grouping sets results with volatile items such as now() stay the same.
The thread disagrees on which commit introduced the crash: 247dea89f or f5050f795ae.

objections.title: Views already stored on 18.x keep the bad substituted tree after the fix
objections.failure_scenario: A user on 18.4 creates a view whose query groups by a constant, such as `group by true` next to `ARRAY[]::varchar(500)[]`. pg_rewrite stores the parse tree with the grouped Var already substituted. After a minor update with this fix, selecting from the view still crashes or still gives the wrong result, because the stored rule is never parsed again.
objections.argument: The fix changes parse analysis in parse_agg.c, so it only affects trees built after the update. CREATE VIEW runs parse analysis but not planning, so the crashing tree from message #1 can already sit in pg_rewrite, as can the wrong-result trees Tom Lane mentions in message #2. pg_upgrade and dump/restore deparse and parse views again, so they repair them, but an in-place minor update does not. The thread does not say whether the fix targets 18, and it gives no note for users on what to recreate.
objections.author_must_show: For back-patched 18 releases, how will views and rules stored with substituted Var-free GROUP BY items be found and repaired, and will the release notes tell users to recreate them?

critic.reasoning: CREATE VIEW stores the analyzed query without planning it, so a view created on 18.x keeps the substituted Var, and a fix in parse_agg.c does not reach it. The thread does not mention stored rules or a release note.

refuted.title: Var-free grouping items stop being nulled in HAVING and other expressions
refuted.failure_scenario: On 18.x, a user runs `select 1+2 as three, count(*) from t group by rollup(three) having (1+2) is null` and gets the grand-total row. After a minor update with v3, the `1+2` in HAVING stays the constant 3, so the row disappears. The user finds out only when a report changes after the update.
refuted.argument: Per message #8, v3 replaces a Var-free item only in the targetlist entry matched by ressortgroupref and skips it in the equal() loop at every sublevel. HAVING and ORDER BY expressions therefore no longer see the nullable grouped Var for such items. Items that contain a Var still go through equal(), so `rollup(a+0)` and `rollup(1+2)` would behave differently in HAVING. Tom Lane's rule in message #4 covers other targetlist entries but not HAVING, and the thread does not say whether the fix goes back to 18.
refuted.author_must_show: Which 18.x query results change under v3, for Var-free grouping items used in HAVING, ORDER BY or subqueries, and is that acceptable in a back-patched minor release?

critic.reasoning: The changed HAVING result is what the rule in message #4 asks for: a Var-free GROUP BY item identifies its targetlist entry "and nothing else". ORDER BY shares that entry through ressortgroupref, and the rollup test in the author claims still returns the null row.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: Views created on 18.x keep the substituted parse tree in pg_rewrite; the patch adds no catalog change itself.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: The patch changes which subexpressions parse_agg.c turns into grouped Vars, so the planner receives different trees.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The fix removes a backend crash that any user can trigger without table access.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The bug exists in released Postgres 18, and the thread does not say whether the fix goes back to 18.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a second matching rule for Var-free items to the grouping code in parse_agg.c.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is v3 meant for back-patching to 18, and if so, which query results on 18.x change after the minor update?
How will views and rules stored on 18.x with a substituted Var-free GROUP BY item be found, and will the release notes tell users to recreate them?
Does skipping Var-free items at every sublevel change results when the GROUP BY item is an outer reference or sits in a correlated subquery?
Do grouping sets queries with volatile Var-free items such as now() return the same results before and after v3?

committability.owner_note: Tom Lane proposed the rule in the thread but has not commented on any patch version; the owner must know the RTE_GROUP substitution code in parse_agg.c.
committability.liability: The owner signs for query results of grouping by Var-free items on 18 and later, including any result change a minor release brings to existing queries.
committability.author_follow_up: Two authors revised the patch through v3, and one fixed a test after a cfbot failure.

priority.reason: The trigger is narrow, but the result is a backend crash in a released branch, with possible wrong answers per message #2. The first patch is 4 KiB in parse_agg.c plus tests; v2 and v3 were not read.

provisional_note: Only 3 of 11 messages and the prose of the first patch were visible. Whether v3 handles outer references, subqueries and volatile items correctly cannot be judged without the code.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: remove_useless_groupby_columns is too enthusiastic
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change remove_useless_groupby_columns so that it no longer removes GROUP BY items that are functionally dependent on a primary key when those items also appear in ORDER BY. This keeps the link between the GROUP BY and ORDER BY lists, so the planner can use a sorted index path with GroupAggregate and avoid an explicit sort.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers pointed out that keeping the redundant columns can make plans worse. Without a matching index, the extra sort columns cost more (Richard Guo measured a slowdown). Hash Aggregate would always pay for hashing and comparing the extra columns. David Rowley proposed a different design: mark redundant GROUP BY columns instead of removing them, and consider both the full and the minimal key sets. No revised patch followed, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback after the thread had been idle for some weeks following that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So the
patch makes that case worse in favour of possibly making Group
Aggregate cases better.

precedents_retrieved.title: Rename constants in preparation of variableness
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series splits each of the 4 page-size-dependent constants into a Cluster variant, meant to become a run-time variable, and a Limit variant holding the maximum value for static allocations. The values stay the same, so behaviour does not change; it prepares for the reserved page space work and was offered for back-branches too.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No one reviewed the design in the visible messages. In August 2024 Kirill Reshke noted that the patch set needed a rebase, asked whether the author would continue, and asked for more informative commit messages. The visible thread shows no reply from the author before the entry was returned with feedback in October 2024.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Your patchset needs a rebase. Are you going to push it forward?

precedents_retrieved.title: Replace literal 0 values with the appropriate Invalid* constants
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace literal 0 values with the matching Invalid* constants (InvalidMultiXactId, InvalidOffsetNumber, InvalidAttrNumber, InvalidDsaPointer, InvalidRelFileNumber) across about 30 files. A Coccinelle script generated the changes, following the earlier InvalidXLogRecPtr cleanup in ec317440716.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that such wholesale cleanup patches add more noise than they improve the code and use review bandwidth better spent elsewhere. He said these changes are fine when the code is edited for other reasons. The author agreed the changes add little value and withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think we should reject these and other similar patches, they generate way
more noise than they are improving the code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallel grouping sets
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add parallel execution of GROUPING SETS queries by splitting aggregation into partial and final stages, first by grouping on the union of all grouping columns in workers and doing the grouping-sets aggregation in the leader. The later version instead performs grouping-sets aggregation in workers, tags each partial tuple with a grouping set ID, and has the leader combine results per grouping set, with refactoring of nodeAgg.c (phase reorganisation, sorting inside the Agg node).
precedents_retrieved.objection: The last patch version received no review and no longer applied to HEAD. A PGCon hallway-track discussion of the approach concluded that nodeAgg.c needs refactoring before it is complicated further, and after an off-list discussion with Melanie, who had picked up the patch, the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There was also considerable discussion in a (virtual) hallway-track session
during PGCon which reviewed the approach (for lack of a better description),
deeming that nodeAgg.c needs a refactoring before complicating it further.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix GROUP BY ALL handling of ORDER BY operator semantics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes GROUP BY ALL copy operator information from matching ORDER BY items, as explicit GROUP BY already does in transformGroupClauseExpr(). It does this by moving that logic into a shared helper, so that `group by all order by a using operator(pg_catalog.*<)` groups rows the same way as `group by a`.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane judged that the patch adds another layer to clause-handling code that grouping sets had already made confusing, and he suspected other bugs of the same kind. He proposed a redesign of that code, which is too large a change after beta2, and suggested reverting GROUP BY ALL for v19 instead. Daniel Gustafsson agreed and posted a revert patch, and the author withdrew the fix.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Chao's patch as proposed doesn't clean any of that up, but just adds
another layer of impenetrability to the logic.

precedents_retrieved.title: GUC-ify WALSender's MAX_SEND_SIZE constant
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch turns the walsender constant MAX_SEND_SIZE (128kB) into a GUC, wal_sender_max_send_size, capped at wal_segment_size. The aim was larger WAL reads per walsender iteration on storage with high latency and high bandwidth, such as Ceph RBD volumes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that the GUC is one more setting nobody can realistically tune, and that it is a poor proxy for the real issue: read size against high-latency storage, better solved by read_stream support for reading WAL. Jakub Wartak agreed and asked for a reproducible benchmark. The author had left the company and could not provide numbers, so Michael Paquier marked the patch rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think it's a bad idea to make it configurable. It's just one more guc that
nobody has a chance of realistically tuning.

precedents_retrieved.title: group locking
precedents_retrieved.summary: Robert Haas proposed a heavyweight-lock concept of "locking groups" for parallelism: a user backend and its worker backends would form a group whose lock requests never conflict with each other, with changes to lock acquisition, wait-queue handling and the deadlock detector so that no group member waits behind an unrelated process. The posted patch was an incomplete draft (LockAcquireExtended() and ProcSleep() modified, ProcWakeup() and the deadlock detector not) meant to get feedback on the design.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the leader could hold the locks for its workers, and that the proposal added too much complexity, with bugs and performance costs, to the lock manager. Andres Freund objected that letting group members hold self-exclusive locks at the same time removes guarantees that existing code relies on, citing transaction abort (smgrDoPendingDeletes) and relcache invalidation. Robert Haas then dropped the original design because it would put too much coordination burden on the workers, and moved to granting the leader's existing locks to workers at the start of a parallel operation. The visible thread ends without agreement on that alternative or a revised patch, and the closing decision is not shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Based on your arguments and those of others, I have long-since abandoned the original proposal of having locks within a group never conflict.

precedents_retrieved.title: rewriteGraphTable: Fix missing RTEs in FROM clause by setting inFromCl=true
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets inFromCl = true on the range table entries that rewriteGraphTable creates for GRAPH_TABLE queries, so that deparsed queries list those relations in the FROM clause. The author wanted this so extensions such as pg_pgq2sql and pg_duckdb can get runnable SQL for graph queries through pg_get_querydef.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. A quoted reply from Ashutosh notes that the subquery RTEs added for views during rewriting have inFromCl = false and suggests a second solution, which the author answered with a use-case argument and a UNION test. The entry was later withdrawn, and the thread shows no decision.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit ef38a4d9756db9ae1d20f40aa39f3cf76059b81a which
implemented the GROUP BY ALL syntax, as well as 2ce745836 which
made some comment improvements therein.

A postcommit review discovered that GROUP BY ALL missed our special
handling of entries that also appear in an ORDER BY in the query.
This caused the query to return wrong results when ORDER BY
specifies non-default equality semantics.  While this should be
fixable with some refactoring, doing it cleanly seems like too
much code churn for late beta.  We'll revert and try again in v20.

The reverted commit also included some additional comment wordsmithing
and docs cleanup, which are retained as they weren't connected to the
reverted feature.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P5] fixed GROUP BY ALL operator semantics in transformGroupClauseExpr(), and its withdrawal was tied to GROUP BY ALL being reverted for v19; this crash fix in substitute_grouped_columns_mutator() shares only the area. The thread cites earlier work only as commits 247dea89f and f5050f795ae (message #1, message #3), which are the source of the bug and not rejected attempts.
The patch adds no syntax, GUC, catalog entry or dump-visible state. The only contract concern from this angle is the change in result semantics for Var-free grouping items.
The patch adds no WAL records, on-disk format change, protocol change or new catalog column. The only persistent state it touches is the parse trees already stored in pg_rewrite.

The fix changes only which GROUP BY items parse_agg.c turns into grouped Vars; it adds no privilege, role, function, GUC, or new exposure. The current bug lets any user who can run a query crash a backend with no table access, so the patch removes an unprivileged denial of service and adds none.

From the maintenance and fit angle there is no objection worth sending. This is a fix for a planner crash in a released branch, and it belongs in core. Its cost is a parse-time Bitmapset and a ressortgroupref check, with no executor or hot-path work. The v2/v3 rule depends on what an item contains, not on its node type. That is more general than the first patch, and future expression nodes with template fields do not have to be listed. [P5] does not apply: its recorded reason concerns GROUP BY ALL and ORDER BY operator handling, which is different code. Committability is the weak point, and it is a separate matter from the verdict. No committer has reviewed v2 or v3, and Tom Lane has not replied to the direct request in message #7. Whether the change is safe to back-patch to 18 is open. That includes Var-free items such as outer references being skipped at every sublevel, and this cannot be checked without the code.

This is a fix for a planner crash and possible wrong results in Postgres 18. No existing feature, setting, contrib module or extension can replace a parser bug fix, so this angle has nothing to raise. P5 is about GROUP BY ALL operator semantics, and its recorded reason does not apply here.

This is a bug fix for a reported SIGSEGV in the planner on Postgres 18 (message #1), with a reproducer and a backtrace. A committer agrees that even non-crashing cases may return wrong answers (message #2), so the demand is real and nobody would ask for more evidence of it. The cost falls on the parse_agg.c code path, not on a new user-facing feature, so a demand objection does not apply.
